To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antioxidant capacity of the retina is significantly enhanced by combining different antioxidants.
the retina is a rich source of lipid peroxidative damage, that the ROS are particularly susceptible to lipid peroxidation, and that the retina has a high capacity for antioxidant protection.

(i) lipid peroxidation can be initiated in retinal tissue and ROS by a combination of Fe and ADP; (ii) TBARS is a useful marker of LHP in retina, ROS, and RPE; and (iii) the AOX palm oil vitamin E is the best inhibitor of lipid peroxidization in retina, ROS or RPE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new antioxidants, the elucidation of the mechanisms of antioxidant action and the determination of the antioxidant capacity of natural products and their constituents.
the development of a simple, rapid and reproducible in vitro model system for the study of the protective effect of AOX on lipid peroxidation and oxidative damage in retinal tissues and cells.
the development of an in vitro system for the study of the effects of antioxidants and other agents in the prevention or treatment of retinal diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in vitro model system is an excellent tool for screening and ranking of antioxidants in terms of their ability to inhibit lipid peroxidation.
vitamin E is an important AOX for retina.
the in vitro model system is a valid model for the study of the antioxidant capacity in bovine retina.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a combination of antioxidants may be a useful therapeutic approach in the prevention of oxidative damage to the eye.
a combination of antioxidants is more efficient than a single one, but that the combination of antioxidants should be chosen with respect to their specific antioxidant properties.
the in vitro system is useful for the evaluation of AOX and that the TBARS and Hb-MB methods are useful biochemical end-point determinations for lipid peroxidation and LHP, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a model system to test AOX in vitro and to show their efficacy.
the in vitro model can be used as a rapid and accurate method to determine the efficacy of a single antioxidant, or to show synergistic effects of combinations of antioxidants.
the use of a combination of AOX may be more beneficial than the use of a single agent.
